nodes.name: Vic Vox
nodes.summary: Victario 'Vic' Vox, one of the two Vox twin bosses of the Heist unique contract 'Contract: The Twins'. Member of the Vox family, descendant of Cardinal Sanctus Vox, named after the poet Victario. After Kurai steals the book 'O' Eternal' for a client he declares war on her, kidnaps and kills her cat Hana, and is killed with his twin by Kurai and the Exile.

sources.locator: 'The Negotiation', 'Returned To Rogue Harbour' and 'The Twins' sections

nodes.name: Vinny Vox
nodes.summary: Vincent 'Vinny' Vox, twin brother of Vic Vox and co-boss of 'Contract: The Twins'. Descendant of Cardinal Sanctus Vox and member of the Vox family; the wiki states the Exile and Kurai kill both twins in the final contract.

nodes.name: Vox family
nodes.summary: Oriathan nobility that became a criminal enterprise; the wiki describes the twins Vic and Vinny Vox using coercion, blackmail and violence to hold a place at the centre of Oriath business and social life. Descended from Cardinal Sanctus Vox.

nodes.name: O' Eternal
nodes.summary: First-edition book written by the Eternal Empire poet Victario. Victario gave a signed copy to Queen Hyrri of Ngamakanui after the battle against General Lioneye; the book later sat in an Oriathan nobleman's vault (the Vox family), was stolen under Kurai's contract 'Hyrri's Gift' for a client, and became the object of the Negotiation and the Vox vendetta.

sources.locator: 'Hyrri's Gift' and 'The Negotiation' sections; Lore paragraph

nodes.name: Contract: Trial Run (Rogue Harbour)
nodes.summary: Kurai's first job for the Ring in the Rogue Harbour introductory quest: after Kurai hands out the contract the Exile speaks to the rogue Karst, opens a portal to the contract zone via Adiyah, completes the contract and sells the Heist target to Faustus. Kurai is first accessible in Act 6 from patch 3.13.0.

chronology.relative: 3.12.0 Heist league quest; Kurai from Act 6 (3.13.0)

sources.locator: Walkthrough: 'Take the Contract: Trial Run from Kurai' to 'Sell the Heist target to Faustus'

nodes.name: Contract: Hyrri's Gift
nodes.summary: Kurai's client contract to retrieve 'O' Eternal', the book Victario gifted Queen Hyrri, from an Oriathan nobleman's vault. The Exile completes the theft; Kurai then promises to return the book to Ngamakanui. The theft leads to Vic Vox's grievance against Kurai.

sources.locator: 'Hyrri's Gift' section (Kaom/Hyrri background and contract text); Lore paragraph

nodes.name: Contract: The Negotiation
nodes.summary: Kurai and the Exile travel to meet the Vox twins over the stolen 'O' Eternal. Kurai says the book is no longer in her possession; Vic Vox declares war on her and the meeting ends with the Vox twins at war with Kurai. Hana, Kurai's cat, is taken afterwards.

sources.locator: 'The Negotiation' section (In-Quest Text) and 'Returned To Rogue Harbour'

nodes.name: Contract: The Rescue
nodes.summary: The Vox twins offer to return Hana and negotiate a truce if Kurai and the Exile meet them in person again. The second meeting ends in hostility (Kurai's counter-proposal is to kill both twins); afterwards Kurai learns the Vox twins killed Hana, and The Boss orders the Vox family dead.

sources.locator: 'The Rescue' section and 'Return To Rogue Harbour' ('They killed Hana')
'Lore': Vic kidnaps and later slaughters Hana

nodes.name: Contract: The Twins
nodes.summary: Final contract of Kurai's questline (unique, tradeable, restartable): Kurai and the Exile strike the Vox twins after Ring intelligence that the twins will unite for a celebration, and kill Vic Vox and Vinny Vox at the Mansion. The Boss authorises a bonus for the Exile.

sources.locator: 'The Twins' sections (Kurai contract four), 'Vic Vox' and 'Vinny Vox' monster boxes
monster box (location Mansion; quest Contract: The Twins); lead

nodes.name: Tempest
nodes.summary: Tempests are effects introduced by Tempest league that can change monster and player size, cause damage, alter drop rates, or animate weapons that drop; affected areas are shown on the World Screen.

nodes.name: Shrine (Domination)
nodes.summary: Shrines are a mechanic introduced by Domination league (1.0.0); Domination's area modifier allowed shrines to spawn.

sources.locator: lead: 'This league introduced shrines'; Modifier section

nodes.name: Strongbox
nodes.summary: Strongboxes are a mechanic introduced by Ambush league (1.1.0, March 2014); every area in Ambush carried the Ambush chests modifier.

nodes.name: Nemesis modifier
nodes.summary: Nemesis modifiers were powerful extra modifiers on every rare monster in Nemesis league (hardcore); the league modifier was "Rare Monsters each have a Nemesis Mod".

nodes.name: Bloodline modifier
nodes.summary: Bloodline modifiers were shared modifiers on each pack of magic monsters in Bloodlines league; they could affect combat while the pack lived and after it died.

nodes.name: Abaxoth, the End of All That Is
nodes.summary: Unique Beyond demon that dual-wields two Edges of Madness and uses Ice Spear with Greater Multiple Projectiles, Vaal Storm Call and Summon Skeletons; it was introduced in 1.2.0 with the Beyond demons and removed in 3.19.0, when Beyond demons were replaced by Scourge monsters.

sources.locator: infobox and lead; Version History (1.2.0 introduced, 3.19.0 removed)
lead: 'Rampage league ... ran concurrently with Beyond league' (1.2.0)

nodes.name: Mutewind (warband)
nodes.summary: One of the three Warbands in Warbands league, alongside Brinerot and Redblades; the wiki calls them the Peak-dwellers. Their outcast Qianga delivered the Starforge to the Watchers of Decay for the Order of the Djinn. Mutewind Warbands also appear as bosses in the Delve map Frozen Hollow.

sources.locator: Warbands item list: Mutewind Wildrunner, Mutewind Lynx, Mutewind Seal
Qianga entry: 'a Mutewind warband outcast'; 'The Mutewind|Peak-dwellers'

nodes.name: The Beachhead
nodes.summary: The Beachhead is a map (several variants, e.g. Red tier and Infused) that holds the Harbinger Portal; defeating the final King Harbinger in any variant drops the unique Harbinger item pieces.

sources.locator: 'Unique pieces' and 'Harbinger scroll' sections; src_poewiki_harbinger_league 'Unique items' section

nodes.name: Sacred Blossom
nodes.summary: Map fragment that opens a portal to The Sacred Grove, where Oshabi, Avatar of the Grove can be encountered. Usable once in a personal Map Device. Drops from tier 4 Harvest bosses (Ersi, Janaar, Namharim); the Heart of the Grove atlas passive stopped always dropping it in 3.19.0.

sources.locator: lead: 'must use a Sacred Blossom in the map device'

nodes.name: An Audience With The King
nodes.summary: Map fragment that grants access to The King in the Mists boss fight at the Crux of Nothingness; it can appear as a reward from Ritual encounters and was added in 3.25.0.

nodes.name: The Menagerie
nodes.summary: Act 2 location unlocked by completing Einhar's Hunt; Einhar gives the optional Einhar's Menagerie quest here (perform beastcrafting once).

sources.locator: Rewards and 'Quest Complete - You have unlocked the Menagerie'

nodes.name: Einhar's Bestiary (Bestiary league quest)
nodes.summary: Act 1 optional quest exclusive to Bestiary league (3.2.0): Einhar Frey on The Coast asks the Exile to capture a beast with a net and keep a bestiary entry for each capture; he claims 'the animals in this land are sick'. Removed in 3.3.0.

sources.locator: Walkthrough: 'Meet hunter-scavenger Einhar Frey on The Coast' to 'Quest Complete - You have unlocked the Bestiary'; Version history 3.2.0/3.3.0

nodes.name: Einhar's Hunt
nodes.summary: Optional Act 2 quest: started by Einhar Frey (Forest Encampment) and played in The Riverways, where the Exile captures all beasts; completing it unlocks The Menagerie.

sources.locator: quest infobox (start: Forest Encampment; completion: capture all beasts in The Riverways) and 'Walkthrough'

Ambush and Invasion ran concurrently from March 5 to July 5, 2014; Ambush used standard death rules and Invasion hardcore.
The wiki says Ambush league introduced Strongboxes.
Domination and Nemesis ran concurrently from October 23, 2013 to February 23, 2014; Nemesis was hardcore.
The wiki says Domination league introduced shrines.
Onslaught and Anarchy ran concurrently from June 7 to October 7, 2013 (Onslaught hardcore, Anarchy standard).
The wiki says Anarchy league introduced rogue exiles.
Rampage and Beyond ran concurrently from August 20 to November 20, 2014; Rampage was standard, Beyond hardcore.
Abaxoth was introduced to the game in 1.2.0, the release that launched Rampage and Beyond.
Abaxoth was removed in 3.19.0, the version that replaced the original Beyond demons with Scourge monsters.
